text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert 2112345678 — p99 latency breach on dedicated-pool-9 in us-west-2. Current p99=2.5s (SLO=800ms). Queue depth > 900 for 5m. Paging oncall@eng-sre.

marta: I see streaming stalls reported by multiple apps, looks tied to dedicated-pool-9. Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/serve/dedicated-pool-9 (logs & traces).

ashwin: +1 seeing lots of KV cache misses and warmup failures. tail latency spikes align with new burst at 09:12 UTC.

liam: grabbing logs now. Are autoscaler events firing?

ashwin: autoscaler initiated scale at 09:13 but warmup window (60s) plus GPU init means pods not Ready until ~09:15. Meanwhile queue kept growing, streaming sessions timed out.

jana: to confirm, this is dedicated capacity (reserved) — not hosted, right? Customers on dedicated saw degraded streaming.

marta: correct. Dedicated-pool-9 is a reserved tenant pool. Some requests routed to fallback model but many routes pinned to specific model version with no fallback.

carlos: quick customer impact summary for SRE->support: two top-tier customers (cust-a, cust-b) reported SSE disconnects and partial responses. No data leak.

support-bot: Notifying account teams for cust-a and cust-b.

liam: logs (truncated):
```
[09:12:21] request_id=rx92 pool=dedicated-pool-9 queuelen=1200 decode_ms=10 service_ms=2500 stream_write_error=timeout
[09:12:42] autoscaler: scale_up request for pool=dedicated-pool-9 target_replicas=6 current=2 reason=queue_depth
[09:12:47] worker init start gpu=0 image_pull=OK hw_setup=ok
[09:13:58] worker ready replicas=3
[09:14:05] queue_depth=400 p99=650ms
[09:14:30] p99=2.2s queue_depth=700
```

nanya: looks like partial scale happened(2->3) but then more burst. Warmup parallelism limited by warmup budget settings. Also cold model KV caches for new workers.

marta: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) increase warmup parallelism and reduce warmup throttle for this pool, 2) temporarily route non-critical traffic to smaller model variant, 3) enable burst-capacity override (if available) for this tenant, 4) proactively run warmup/jit on new replicas. Thoughts?

ashwin: I can flip routing rules to fallback model for lower-priority routes in 30s. That should cut queue by ~30-40%. Doing it now: `/orchestrator route set-priority --pool dedicated-pool-9 --priority low --model small-gpt-neo-quant`

incident-bot: Command received: route change queued by ashwin.

liam: I'll manually bump pool target to 8 to soak the burst while we warmup. `/autoscaler set-target --pool dedicated-pool-9 --replicas 8 --reason "incident: burst"`

sre-bot: autoscaler override applied by liam. New target=8. Warmup budget increase recommended.

carlos: Support note: informing cust-a that we are actively mitigating and will provide postmortem.

jana: After routing fallback and manual scale, are we seeing p99 drop?

ashwin: preliminary numbers: p95 dropped to 420ms after reroute and a few workers came up. p99 still at ~1.1s but trending down. Queue depth 200.

marta: good. We should also open a short-lived throttle on large-batch endpoints to reduce decode pressure. Proposal: limit batch_size > 1024 requests for 5m.

anya: I'm running a warmup job to prefill KV caches on new workers. Command: `/infra warmup --pool dedicated-pool-9 --replicas 6 --model-version v2026-03-10`

incident-bot: Warmup job started (job-id=wup-211234). Logs: warmup requests/s=150, cache-fill=ok.

liam: Observability update: streaming stalls decreased, error-rate for SSE=2.1% -> 0.6% in last 5m. p99=780ms now. Still above target slightly but within degradation window.

marta: handoff: I'm going offline for a deploy in 10m. @liam please take incident lead. If anything regresses, page eng-sre again.

liam: taking lead. I'll keep monitoring until steady state.

ashwin: routing revert plan: once p99 < 600ms and queue < 100 for 5m, route back to primary model and reduce replicas back to baseline (3). We'll do gradual traffic shift.

carlos: I updated incident channel with customer impact doc: https://docs.redwood.example/incidents/2112345678-impact — includes timeline and affected routes.

support-bot: Cust-a notified: interim mitigation applied. ETA for full restore 30m.

jana: follow-up action items (post-incident):
- Reduce warmup window or allow faster init paths for dedicated pools.
- Improve autoscaler aggressiveness threshold when queue depth > 500.
- Add automated warmup preflight when autoscaler scales beyond +2 replicas.
- Add route-level fallback policy that can be enabled per-tenant.

marta: +1 on those. Also we should add an SLO burn chart to the alert to avoid cascading pages for transient spikes.

anya: I'll file a runbook PR to add a manual override checklist for dedicated pools (warmup, fallback, manual scale).

liam: system metrics now: p95=340ms p99=610ms queue=85 replicas=6 ready=6 streaming_errors=0.4%

marta: great progress. I'll join in 30m for postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident 2112345678 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigning postmortem owners: jana (lead), anya (docs), ashwin (infra follow-ups).

liam: closing handoff: leaving channel to Jana for post-incident.

jana: acknowledged, taking ownership. I'll schedule a 30-min RCA sync in 2 hours.

sre-bot: Reminder: capture traces and retain logs for 90 days for this incident.

marta: thank you.
